seo.title: Turso and libSQL client for {devices}
seo.description: Open Turso databases by URL and token, self-hosted sqld servers or libSQL files on your Mac. Query in SQLite syntax; change tables, indexes and triggers.

header.title: Turso and libSQL client
header.lead: Connect to a Turso database with its URL and token, or open a libSQL file, and query it in SQLite’s syntax.

bands.title: Connect to Turso
text: Choose <ui>Remote (Turso)</ui> in <ui>Connection Mode</ui>, then paste the database’s HTTPS URL and an <ui>API Token</ui>, which is stored in the macOS Keychain. Both come from the Turso dashboard or CLI.
An imported libsql:// URL becomes an HTTPS remote connection, and each URL names one database. Plain HTTP URLs are not encrypted, and SSH tunnels are not available.

bands.title: Query and edit
text: libSQL speaks SQLite’s syntax, so browsing, <explain>EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN</explain> diagrams and export behave as they do on <sqlite>SQLite</sqlite>.

A remote connection runs no transaction: each statement is its own HTTP request and commits on its own, and BEGIN fails with “Transactions are not supported in this mode”. Transactions need a local file, opened as libSQL. Remote mode loads no SQLite extensions, since a Turso database runs the ones its server was built with, and a throttled request’s error says how many seconds to wait.

bands.title: Tables, indexes and triggers
text: The <structure>Structure tab</structure> creates tables, adds and drops columns and indexes, and creates, edits and drops triggers. Tables, but not views, can be renamed from the sidebar.
A remote column reorder or foreign key change produces a rebuild script for you to review and run, because TablePro cannot hold separate HTTP requests in one transaction.

family.title: libSQL
text: Choose libSQL for a self-hosted sqld server, reached through its Hrana v2 pipeline endpoint, or for a file on this Mac in <ui>Local File</ui> mode. A local file runs transactions, loads SQLite extensions and runs rebuild scripts once you confirm them, and <backup>Backup Dump and Restore Dump</backup> run {dumpTool} on it.
Never open a file that a running app syncs as a Turso embedded replica: access from two programs at once can corrupt it.

moveData: <export>Export</export> a table or a query result as {exportFormats}. To load data, use the Turso CLI or an import on your sqld server.

faq.question: Should I pick Remote or Local File?
faq.answer: Remote, for a Turso database or a sqld server you reach by URL. Local File, for a libSQL file on this Mac, which also gives you transactions, SQLite extensions and backups.

faq.question: Do I need the Turso CLI installed?
faq.answer: No. The Turso dashboard shows the database URL and creates tokens too. The CLI is useful for loading data from the terminal.
